slide_title: Artificial Reproduction Strategies: Meristem, Anther & Suspension Culture
original_text: Artificial Reproduction Strategies Meristem tissue Results in clonal plants with identical traits Anther tissue culture Haploid cells in pollen grains are cultured to produce haploid plantlets A diploid plantlet can be produced by adding a chemical agent that encourages chromosome doubling Cell Suspension Culture Rapidly growing calluses are cut into small pieces and shaken into a liquid nutrient medium Single cells or small clumps break off and form a suspension Used to extract chemicals and metabolites, many times which have been genetically modified, from plant cells.
explanation: This slide describes three specialized tissue culture techniques: 1) Meristem culture: uses virus-free apical meristem tissue to produce clonal plants with identical genetic traits. 2) Anther tissue culture: involves culturing the haploid cells inside pollen grains to produce haploid plantlets. To make these plants fertile and diploid, scientists add a chemical agent that encourages chromosome doubling. 3) Cell suspension culture: involves taking rapidly growing cell masses (calluses), cutting them into small pieces, and shaking them in a liquid nutrient medium. Single cells or small clumps break off to form a suspension, which is used to extract valuable chemicals and metabolic products, often from genetically modified plant cells.

questions.q: During anther culture, how can a fertile diploid plantlet be generated from haploid pollen cells?
opts: By performing double fertilization in a test tube
By adding a chemical agent that encourages chromosome doubling in haploid plantlets
By grafting the haploid stem onto a diploid rootstock
By growing the plantlets in a medium rich in Rhizobium bacteria
questions.exp: Anther culture initially produces haploid plantlets. A chemical agent is then applied to encourage chromosome doubling, producing fertile diploid plants.

questions.q: What is the procedure for establishing a cell suspension culture?
opts: Grafting a shoot apical meristem onto a root system in liquid soil
Culturing whole flowers in an anaerobic gas chamber
Shaking pieces of rapidly growing callus tissue in a liquid nutrient medium to break off single cells
Extracting seeds and placing them in cold weather to break dormancy
questions.exp: Cell suspension culture is created by cutting calluses into pieces and shaking them in a liquid nutrient medium, causing single cells or small clumps to break off into suspension.
